ATLANTIC BASIN BEST TRACK DOCUMENTATION............BY CHRIS LANDSEA (2/16/95)

This documentation is based upon "A tropical cyclone data tape for the
North Atlantic basin, 1886-1983:  Contents, limitations, and uses", _NOAA
Technical Memorandum NWS NHC 22_, 1984 written by B.R. Jarvinen, C.J. 
Neumann, and M.A.S. Davis.  The North Atlantic 'best track' (so named as it
is the 'best' track and intensity estimates of tropical cyclones as 
determined in a post-analysis of all available data) is maintained by the
forecasters and researchers at the National Hurricane Center in Miami, 
Florida.  Permission to make free access of this data and documentation
were provided by Dr. Robert Sheets - director of NHC and by Mr. Neal Lott
of the National Climatic Data Center in Asheville, NC.  Questions 
regarding the format and/or errors in the documentation/data should be
directed to Chris Landsea (landsea@downdry.atmos.colostate.edu).

Currently, the database extends from 1886 to 1993.  The database filename
is 'tra86to93.atl.  Updates for the coming year will be provided as soon 
as the analysis is final at NHC.  So, I hope this data provides some 
insight into the workings of the Atlantic hurricane for you as it, to some
degree, has for me........CWL

Note that the 'tra86to93.atl' file is UNIX compressed to save space on
our computer so that the filename is 'tra86to93.atl.Z'.  To read the file 
after you've ftp'ed it, you need to UNCOMPRESS the file.  Otherwise, you 
can't access the data.

$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$

P.S.  Though the data extends back to 1886, one is cautioned in deriving
seasonal statistics back that many years.  The advent of aircraft reconn-
aissance in 1944 is suggested (both by myself and C.J. Neumann) to be the
start of reliable seasonal statistics on the frequency and duration of
storms.  However, as reported in Landsea (1993) ["A climatology of intense
(or major) Atlantic hurricanes", _Mon. Wea. Rev._, 121, 1703-1713], there
is a bias in the best track data in that strong hurricanes were over-
reported in windstrength for the years 1944 to 1969 (and possibly before
1944 as well).  This bias amounted to a five knot overestimation at the 
100kt threshold for major hurricane status.  The amount of overestimation 
is even worse for yet stronger storms.

$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$$

There are three basic types of datalines in the Best Track.  

TYPE A:
92620 08/16/1992 M=13  2 SNBR= 899 ANDREW      XING=1 SSS=4
Card# MM/DD/Year Days S# Total#... Name........US Hit.Hi US category

TYPE B:
92580 04/22S2450610  30 1003S2490615  45 1002S2520620  45 1002S2550624  45 1003*
Card# MM/DD&LatLongWindPress&LatLongWindPress&LatLongWindPress&LatLongWindPress

TYPE C:
92760 HRCFL4BFL3 LA3
Card# TpHit.Hit.Hit.

..........................................................................

TYPE A:

   Card# = Sequential card number starting at 00010 in 1886

   MM/DD/Year = Month, Day, and Year of storm

   Days = Number of days in which positions are available (note that this
          also means number of lines to follow of type B and then one line
          of type C)

   S# = Storm number for that particular year (including subtropical storms)

   Total# = Storm number since the beginning of the record (since 1886)

   Name = Storms only given official names since 1950

   US Hit = '1' = Made landfall over the United States as tropical
                  storm or hurricane,
            '0' = did not make U.S. landfall 

   Hi US category = '9' = Used before 1899 to indicate U.S. landfall as a
                          hurricane of unspecified Saffir-Simpson category
                    '0' = Used to indicate U.S. landfall as tropical storm,
                          but this has not been utilized in recent years
                    '1' to '5' = Highest category on the Saffir-Simpson scale
                                 that the storm made landfall along the U.S.
                                 '1' is a minimal hurricane, '5' is a 
                                 catastrophic hurricane
...........................................................................

TYPE B:

   Card# = As above.
 
   MM/DD = Month and Day of Storm

   & = 'S' (Subtropical stage), '*' (tropical cyclone stage),
       'E' (extratropical stage), 'W' (wave stage - rarely used)

   LatLong = Position of storm:  24.5N, 61.0W

   Wind = Maximum sustained (1 minute) surface (10m) windspeed in knots (in
          general, these are to the nearest 5 knots).

   Press = Central surface pressure of storm in mb (if available).  Since
           1979, central pressures are given everytime even if a satellite
           estimation is needed.

   Positions and intensities are at 00Z, 06Z, 12Z, 18Z

..........................................................................

TYPE C:

   Card# = As above.
 
   Tp = Maximum intensity of storm ('HR' = hurricane, 'TS' = tropical

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Otis_2023-10-25_0430Z.jpg/250px-Otis_2023-10-25_0430Z.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Otis_2023-10-25_0430Z.jpg)

Satellite image of [Hurricane Otis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Otis "Hurricane Otis"), the strongest [Pacific hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_hurricane "Pacific hurricane") to ever hit Mexico

The [North American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America "North America") country of [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico") regularly experiences [tropical cyclones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone "Tropical cyclone") from both the [Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean") and the [Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean") oceans. Tropical cyclones that produce [maximum sustained winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_sustained_wind "Maximum sustained wind") of more than 119[kilometre per hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilometre_per_hour "Kilometre per hour") (74[mph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miles_per_hour "Miles per hour")) are designated as hurricanes, which can produce deadly and damaging effects, particularly where they make [landfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landfall "Landfall"), or move ashore. Hurricane strength has been ranked using the [Saffir-Simpson scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffir-Simpson_scale "Saffir-Simpson scale") since 1972, from a minimal hurricane as a Category 1 to the most powerful as a Category 5. The most recent Category 5 hurricane to hit Mexico was [Hurricane Otis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Otis "Hurricane Otis") in 2023, which was also the costliest Mexican hurricane.

## Climatology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Mexico_hurricanes&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Climatology")]

From 1951 to 2000, [Pacific hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_hurricanes "Pacific hurricanes") most frequently struck the northwestern Mexican states Baja California Sur or Sinaloa, as well as Michoacán in southern Mexico. [Atlantic hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_hurricanes "Atlantic hurricanes") during the same period were most likely to hit Quintana Roo along the eastern Yucatán peninsula and Veracruz along the [Bay of Campeche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Campeche "Bay of Campeche"). Along both coasts, the month with the most landfalls was September, although they can occur as early as May.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Mexico_hurricanes#cite_note-1)

## List of states

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Mexico_hurricanes&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: List of states")]

The category listed for each state indicates the maximum category of sustained winds that were recorded or analyzed to have occurred in that state. It is not necessarily the category of the storm at the time of landfall or closest approach (if the strongest winds were occurring elsewhere or only over water at the time).

The [North American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America "North America") country of [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico") regularly experiences [tropical cyclones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone "Tropical cyclone") from both the [Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean") and the [Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean") oceans. Tropical cyclones that produce [maximum sustained winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_sustained_wind "Maximum sustained wind") of more than 119[kilometre per hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilometre_per_hour "Kilometre per hour") (74[mph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miles_per_hour "Miles per hour")) are designated as hurricanes, which can produce deadly and damaging effects, particularly where they make [landfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landfall "Landfall"), or move ashore. Hurricane strength has been ranked using the [Saffir-Simpson scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffir-Simpson_scale "Saffir-Simpson scale") since 1972, from a minimal hurricane as a Category 1 to the most powerful as a Category 5. The most recent Category 5 hurricane to hit Mexico was [Hurricane Otis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Otis "Hurricane Otis") in 2023, which was also the costliest Mexican hurricane.

## Climatology

From 1951 to 2000, [Pacific hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_hurricanes "Pacific hurricanes") most frequently struck the northwestern Mexican states Baja California Sur or Sinaloa, as well as Michoacán in southern Mexico. [Atlantic hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_hurricanes "Atlantic hurricanes") during the same period were most likely to hit Quintana Roo along the eastern Yucatán peninsula and Veracruz along the [Bay of Campeche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Campeche "Bay of Campeche"). Along both coasts, the month with the most landfalls was September, although they can occur as early as May.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Mexico_hurricanes&printable=yes#cite_note-1)

## List of states

The category listed for each state indicates the maximum category of sustained winds that were recorded or analyzed to have occurred in that state. It is not necessarily the category of the storm at the time of landfall or closest approach (if the strongest winds were occurring elsewhere or only over water at the time).

# HURDAT 2 - Northeast and North Central Pacific Hurricane Database - NOAA

This dataset was provided on 9 May 2016 to include the remaining 2014 best tracks for Genevieve, Iselle, and Julio in the Central Pacific Hurricane Center (CPHC) area of responsibility. Note that the 2015 best tracks from CPHC are not yet available and are not currently included. Once CPHC completes their post-storm analyses, this dataset will be updated.

This dataset (known as NE/NC Pacific HURDAT2) has a comma-delimited, text format with six-hourly information on the location, maximum winds, central pressure, and (beginning in 2004) size of all known tropical cyclones and subtropical cyclones [HURDAT](https://oasishub.co/dataset/hurdat-2-atlantic-hurricane-database "HURDAT")

Part of the **[2013 Pacific hurricane season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Pacific_hurricane_season "2013 Pacific hurricane season")**

**Hurricane Manuel** ([/ˌ m æ n(j)u ˈ ɛ l,ˌ m ɑː n-/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"))[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-1) was a catastrophic [tropical cyclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone "Tropical cyclone") that brought widespread [flooding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flooding "Flooding") across much of Mexico in September 2013, in conjunction with [Hurricane Ingrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Ingrid "Hurricane Ingrid"). The fifteenth [named storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone_naming "Tropical cyclone naming") and seventh hurricane of the [annual hurricane season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Pacific_hurricane_season "2013 Pacific hurricane season"), Manuel originated from a strong area of [low pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-pressure_area "Low-pressure area") south of [Acapulco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acapulco "Acapulco") on September 13. Within favorable conditions aloft, the storm intensified into a [tropical storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_storm "Tropical storm") as it tracked northward. The following day, Manuel curved westward and strengthened to a point just shy of hurricane intensity before making its first [landfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landfall "Landfall") at that intensity on September 15. Due to interaction with land, the tropical storm quickly weakened, and its center dissipated over western Mexico on September 16. However, the storm's [remnants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-tropical_cyclone "Post-tropical cyclone") continued to track northwestward into the [Gulf of California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_California "Gulf of California"), where they reorganized into a tropical cyclone the next day. Manuel regained tropical storm status on September 18 as it began to curve northeastward. Shortly thereafter, Manuel attained Category 1 hurricane intensity, before making its final landfall just west of [Culiacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culiac%C3%A1n "Culiacán") at peak intensity. Over land, Manuel quickly weakened due to interaction with Mexico's high terrain, and the storm dissipated early on September 20.

Due to the impending threat of Manuel, several Mexican municipalities were put under disaster alerts. Upon making its first landfall, Manuel caused extreme flooding in southern Mexico. Property and agricultural damage as a result of the system was widespread, and roughly one million people were estimated to have been directly affected. In [Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerrero "Guerrero"), 97 people perished, including 18 in [Acapulco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acapulco "Acapulco"). Seventy-one others died due to a mudslide in La Pintada. In Guerrero alone, around 30,000 homes were damaged and 46 rivers overflowed their banks. There, 20,000 persons were evacuated to shelters. Statewide, repairs to damage from the storm totaled [MXN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_peso "Mexican peso")$3 billion ($230 million [USD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Dollar "United States Dollar")).[[nb 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-2) Other impacts from Manuel spread as far east as the [Isthmus of Tehuantepec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isthmus_of_Tehuantepec "Isthmus of Tehuantepec"), where 300 families were displaced. In the region, at least 11,591 homes were destroyed by the floods. Meanwhile, the nation sustained additional impacts from Atlantic [Hurricane Ingrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Ingrid "Hurricane Ingrid").

After its second landfall, additional floods occurred in several towns, and in [Sinaloa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinaloa "Sinaloa") over 100,000 people were rendered homeless and four people died. As a result of Manuel's impacts, 107 municipalities were declared disaster regions. Damage in Sinaloa totaled MXN$500 million (US$37.9 million). The [Mexican Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Army "Mexican Army") was dispatched in several locations to aid in post-tropical cyclone relief operations. Following the storm, looting in heavily impacted areas became commonplace, and as such government forces were also dispatched to prevent further looting. Overall, 169 people lost their lives in Mexico, while damage exceeded MXN$55 billion (US$4.2 billion). Manuel was the costliest Pacific hurricane on record at the time, until it was surpassed by [Hurricane Otis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Otis "Hurricane Otis") in 2023.

The origins of Manuel can be traced back to a [tropical wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_wave "Tropical wave") that left the African continent in late August. The wave entered the Caribbean Sea on September 5, although the northern portion of the wave axis later developed into [Hurricane Ingrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Ingrid "Hurricane Ingrid").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3) On September 10, the [National Hurricane Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hurricane_Center "National Hurricane Center") (NHC) remarked the potential for a [low-pressure area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-pressure_area "Low-pressure area") to [develop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclogenesis "Tropical cyclogenesis") off the southwest coast of Mexico during the subsequent few days, provided the system remained offshore.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-4) The next day, a low formed while it was nearly stationary, accompanied by scattered [convection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convection_(meteorology) "Convection (meteorology)").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-5) Strong [wind shear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_shear "Wind shear") and proximity to land were expected to limit development,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-6) although conditions became more favorable on September 12. On that day, the convection became better organized.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-7) At 1200[UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time "Coordinated Universal Time") on September 13, the NHC initiated advisories on Tropical Depression Thirteen-E,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3) noting that the system had enough of a well-defined [circulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone#Background "Tropical cyclone") and convection. By that time, wind shear had diminished and warm waters were expected to allow intensification, and the main inhibiting factors for development were proximity to land and association with the [Intertropical Convergence Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intertropical_Convergence_Zone "Intertropical Convergence Zone").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-8)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Manuel_Sept_15_2013_1725Z.jpg/250px-Manuel_Sept_15_2013_1725Z.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Manuel_Sept_15_2013_1725Z.jpg)

Tropical Storm Manuel over Western Mexico on September 15

Within a few hours of developing, the depression quickly intensified into Tropical Storm Manuel.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3) By early on September 14, an [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_(cyclone) "Eye (cyclone)") feature developed as [rainbands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainband "Rainband") increased. However, Manuel was embedded within a broad weather system that extended from the eastern Pacific across Mexico, which included Hurricane Ingrid in the [Bay of Campeche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Campeche "Bay of Campeche") on the [Gulf of Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico "Gulf of Mexico") coast. The broad system, including Manuel, moved generally northward.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-9) By early on September 15, Manuel had developed a [central dense overcast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_dense_overcast "Central dense overcast"), with a 17 mi (27 km) wide eye in the center. Based on the structure and satellite-intensity estimates, the NHC estimated Manuel attained secondary peak winds of 70 mph (115 km/h), just shy of hurricane status. The agency noted the potential for further strengthening into a hurricane, citing the warm waters, moist environment, and low shear.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-10) A break in the [subtropical ridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subtropical_ridge "Subtropical ridge") to the north allowed the storm to initially continue generally to the north-northeast, soon peaking as a low-end Category 1 hurricane;[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-11) however, after reaching its peak intensity, Manuel turned back to the northwest while accelerating.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3) On September 15, Manuel made [landfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landfall "Landfall") near [Aquila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquila,_Michoac%C3%A1n "Aquila, Michoacán") in [Michoacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michoac%C3%A1n "Michoacán") as a high-end tropical storm,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3) though operationally, it was believed to have moved ashore near [Manzanillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manzanillo,_Colima "Manzanillo, Colima") in [Colima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colima "Colima").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-12) Early on September 16, the storm weakened into a tropical depression after the circulation became disrupted, although it continued dropping heavy rainfall.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-13) Later that day, the surface center dissipated over western Mexico.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-14)

The remnants of Manuel tracked northwest around a ridge situated over the southeastern United States,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3) and late on September 16, emerged over open waters.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-15) Despite only marginally favorable conditions,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-16) convection soon increased over the center.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3) At 1800 UTC on September 17 Manuel regenerated into a tropical depression after redeveloping a well-defined circulation.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3) Furthermore, conditions favored additional strengthening as the system tracked slowly northwestward around a ridge, although the cyclone was expected to move onshore the [Baja California Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baja_California_Peninsula "Baja California Peninsula") in a few days.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-17) Although the convection was initially ragged,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-18) Manuel re-intensified into a tropical storm on September 18.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-19) Later that day, an eye developed in the center of the increasingly organizing convection,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-20) and at 0000 UTC on September 19, Manuel became a hurricane.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-21) It thus became the first eastern North Pacific tropical cyclone since records began in 1949 to make landfall in mainland Mexico, and later redevelop into a hurricane.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3) The storm shifted more to the north, resulting in land interaction earlier than anticipated.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-22) Around 1200 UTC on September 19, Manuel made landfall just west of [Culiacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culiac%C3%A1n "Culiacán") as a minimal hurricane.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-23) Moving over the high terrain of western Mexico, Manuel quickly weakened into a tropical storm.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-24) The storm's circulation dissipated at 0000 UTC on September 20, over the Sierra Madre Occidental mountain range.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-25)

## Preparations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hurricane_Manuel&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Preparations")]

On the afternoon of September 13, a [tropical storm warning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone_warnings_and_watches "Tropical cyclone warnings and watches") was issued from [Acapulco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acapulco "Acapulco") to [Lázaro Cárdenas, Michoacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A1zaro_C%C3%A1rdenas,_Michoac%C3%A1n "Lázaro Cárdenas, Michoacán"). Thirty-six hours later, a hurricane warning was issued from Lázaro Cárdenas to Manzanillo as the system was expected to become a hurricane prior to landfall. Later on September 15, a tropical storm watch was declared north of the hurricane warning. By early the next day, all watches and warnings were no longer in effect.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3) In addition to the aforementioned watches and warnings, an "orange" alert was issued in southern [Michoacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michoac%C3%A1n "Michoacán"), and "yellow" (moderate) alert was in place for the rest of Michoacán and [Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerrero "Guerrero"). Lower levels of alerts were issued in [Nayarit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nayarit "Nayarit"), [Colima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colima "Colima"), [Jalisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalisco "Jalisco"), Oaxaca, and in the southern portion of [Sinaloa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinaloa "Sinaloa").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EN1-26) Twenty-five families were evacuated in Lázaro Cárdenas, and [Arteaga, Michoacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arteaga_Municipality,_Michoac%C3%A1n "Arteaga Municipality, Michoacán").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU4-27) On September 17, all classes were suspended in [Colima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colima "Colima").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CN6-28)

After regenerating into a tropical cyclone in the Gulf of California, a tropical storm watch was issued just north of [Mazatlán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n "Mazatlán") as well as the southwestern portion of the [Baja California Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baja_California_Peninsula "Baja California Peninsula") The next day, a hurricane watch was issued for the area south of [Topolobampo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topolobampo "Topolobampo"). At 2100 UTC on September 18, the hurricane watch was upgraded into a hurricane warning. Meanwhile, a tropical storm warning was designated south of the hurricane warning area to Mazatlán. On the evening of September 19, all watches and warnings were discontinued, as Manuel had moved inland.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3)

On September 18, when the cyclone first threatened the state, 13 municipalities were placed on alert in Sonora.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU43-29) Along the Baja California Peninsula, seven ports were closed.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU46-30) The ports of [Mazatlán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n "Mazatlán"), [Cabo San Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabo_San_Lucas "Cabo San Lucas"), and [San José del Cabo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jos%C3%A9_del_Cabo "San José del Cabo") were closed for small craft and night interests.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU21-31) A "yellow" alert was issued for southern [Baja California Sur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baja_California_Sur "Baja California Sur") while a "green" alert was issued for the northern portion of the state.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU22-32) In [Sinaloa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinaloa "Sinaloa"), classes were suspended.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU32-33) Prior to landfall, 700 people were evacuated statewide,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU48-34) including 365 residents from two municipalities.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU28-35) Over 60 families were evacuated in [Navolato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navolato,_Sinaloa "Navolato, Sinaloa").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-NPR-36) An "orange" alert was also activated for the state.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU50-37)

Around the same time as Manuel's first landfall, [Hurricane Ingrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Ingrid "Hurricane Ingrid") made landfall along the eastern coast of the nation; this marked the first time two [tropical cyclones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone "Tropical cyclone") struck the nation within 24 hours since [1958](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958_Pacific_hurricane_season "1958 Pacific hurricane season").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW1-48) Overall, economic impact exceeded MXN$55 billion (US$4.2 billion).[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-Steve_Jakubowski-1-49) Damage to roads alone totaled to $2 billion pesos ($153 million 2013 USD).[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CN11-50) A total of 123 people were killed due to Hurricane Manuel, at least of 104 of which were direct.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3) Roughly 59,000 people were evacuated, including 39,000 that sought shelter.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RWES-51) Approximately 1 million people were directly affected by Manuel.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-NBCN-52)

Hurricane Manuel brought extremely heavy rains for eight days over much of Mexico, especially over mountainous terrain, although this precipitation was aided by Ingrid as well as large-scale southwesterly [monsoonal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoonal "Monsoonal") flow. Numerous locations recorded more than 10 in (250 mm) of rain. A peak storm total of 43.6 in (1,110 mm) was measured in [San Isidro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acapulco_(municipality) "Acapulco (municipality)"), Guerrero. In nearby Acapulco, a secondary maximum of 17.8 in (450 mm) was recorded. Further north, in [Michoacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michoac%C3%A1n "Michoacán"), a statewide peak rainfall total of 22.11 in (562 mm) occurred. After making its second landfall, 18.52 in (470 mm) of precipitation fell in [Culiacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culiac%C3%A1n "Culiacán") and 15.32 in (389 mm) was observed in nearby Sanalona.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3)

### Oaxaca

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hurricane_Manuel&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Oaxaca")]

In [Jicayan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jicayan "Jicayan"), Manuel damaged 10 homes and flooded a school. Offshore, one boat was reportedly missing.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU2-53) Along the [Isthmus of Tehuantepec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isthmus_of_Tehuantepec "Isthmus of Tehuantepec"), 300 families were displaced from their homes.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-54) Roughly 5,000 animals were killed by the storm.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CNN3-55) A total of 200 ha (490 acres) of crop was destroyed in [Oaxaca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oaxaca "Oaxaca"); however, damage in the state was considerably less than in Guerrero.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU38-56) Within Oaxaca, 19 communities were isolated.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU40-57) Four people were killed in the state.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CF-58) Overall, 77 municipalities[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW5-59) or 10,000 people were directly affected by the floods.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-SG2-60)

### Guerrero

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hurricane_Manuel&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Guerrero")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/EPN._Afectados_tormenta_Manue_en_Acapulco.jpg/250px-EPN._Afectados_tormenta_Manue_en_Acapulco.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:EPN._Afectados_tormenta_Manue_en_Acapulco.jpg)

President [Enrique Peña Nieto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enrique_Pe%C3%B1a_Nieto "Enrique Peña Nieto") and [Secretary of the Interior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_the_Interior_(Mexico) "Secretary of the Interior (Mexico)")[Miguel Ángel Osorio Chong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_%C3%81ngel_Osorio_Chong "Miguel Ángel Osorio Chong") visit affected zones around [Acapulco de Juárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acapulco_de_Ju%C3%A1rez "Acapulco de Juárez") on 16 September 2013.

At least 97 people were killed throughout Guerrero.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TCR-3) Approximately 30,000 dwellings were damaged,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-BBC_2-61) including 11,591 houses sustained severe damage.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW5-59) Moreover, at least 11,000 homes were destroyed[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TT-62) 20,000 people were evacuated to shelters.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU25-63) 12,000 of which were evacuated to 47 shelters.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TT-62) Overall, 24 rivers flooded,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW5-59) at least 32 roads sustained damage, and four bridges collapsed.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU25-63)

In La Pintada, a remote fishing village of around 400 residents situated to the west of Acapulco,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW4-64) a mudslide occurred on September 14, which within a few minutes, swept through the center of town. As such, many residents initially wandered throughout town in a state of panic and confusion;[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-BBC_2-61) it took two days for word of the mudslide to spread to the public.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW7-65) Throughout the village, 71 people were killed.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-YE-66) Over half the town, including 20 homes, were demolished due to the mudslide. A total of 334 people were evacuated by police,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW4-64) though 30 elected to stay in the area until all the victims had been identified.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW8-67) Many surviving citizens of La Pintada were also hurt, including one seriously.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-USA_Today-68)

In the municipality of Atlamajalcingo, a woman died after a collapse of a dwelling.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU5-69) In [Chilpancingo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilpancingo "Chilpancingo"), the capital of Guerrero, four people perished.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU8-70) Numerous trees were downed and power outages were reported. Additionally, the nearby Cerrito Rico dam nearly overflowed its banks.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU7-71) In the [Tecpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tecp%C3%A1n_de_Galeana_(municipality) "Tecpán de Galeana (municipality)") municipality, four rivers overflowed their banks and six people died because of landslides.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW1-48) Many mountainous communities were isolated, thus making in difficult to receive aid.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-BBC_2-61)

#### Acapulco

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hurricane_Manuel&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Acapulco")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Resultados_del_Hurac%C3%A1n_Ingrid_y_tormenta_Manuel_%28Acapulco%2C_Guerrero%29_23.JPG/250px-Resultados_del_Hurac%C3%A1n_Ingrid_y_tormenta_Manuel_%28Acapulco%2C_Guerrero%29_23.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Resultados_del_Hurac%C3%A1n_Ingrid_y_tormenta_Manuel_(Acapulco,_Guerrero)_23.JPG)

Debris on beach in the [Acapulco Diamante](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acapulco_Diamante?action=edit&redlink=1 "Acapulco Diamante (page does not exist)")[[es](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acapulco%20Diamante "es:Acapulco Diamante")] area.

The city of Acapulco sustained the worst damage from the storm;[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU3-72) the damage in Acapulco was described by the [National Broadcasting Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Broadcasting_Company "National Broadcasting Company") as the "worst storm damage to hit Mexico in years".[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-NBCN-52) There, 18 fatalities occurred,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-IN-73) including one person that died when a wall collapsed.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU5-69) Nearby, six tourists perished in a car crash, including two minors.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU3-72) The crash also damaged two fences, a boat, and injured two people.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU1-74) Several homes were flooded in nearby neighborhoods of Acapulco when a nearby river overflowed its banks.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU1-74) Isolated incidents of vandalism were reported.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW5-59) Two mudslides were reported, resulting in the destruction of a home and the closure of a few roads.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-GI1-75) A family of six perished in Acapulco when a landslide demolished their home.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW1-48) At least 40,000 tourists who spent the [Mexican Independence Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Independence_Day "Mexican Independence Day") in Acapulco were stranded since the terminal of the airport was underwater.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-NBCN-52)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU12-76) Furthermore, the main roads out of the city were blocked by landslides. Even though by September 19, the military had evacuated 10,000 people via 100 flights to Mexico City,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-USA_Today-68) this process was difficult because the [radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radar "Radar") was not functioning.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW2-77) Citywide, 13,516 dwellings were damaged.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CNN3-55)

### Colima

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hurricane_Manuel&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Colima")]

Although flooding was minor in [Colima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colima "Colima"),[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU47-78) a peak rainfall total of 144 mm (5.7 in) was measured in [Chanal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chanal,_Chiapas "Chanal, Chiapas").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CN3-79) Many families were evacuated.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU10-80) Several dams statewide reached their maximum capacity[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU17-81) while numerous roads that led to the Manzanillo airport were closed.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU18-82) In [Ixtlahuacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ixtlahuac%C3%A1n "Ixtlahuacán"), 50 families were evacuated when a river threatened to overflow its banks;[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CN1-83) thirty others were taken to shelter in the rest of the state.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CN5-84) A bridge collapsed in [Villa de Alvarez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa_de_Alvarez "Villa de Alvarez").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CN8-85) One man was killed in the state when he unsuccessfully attempted to cross a river.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU41-86) Four trees were brought down.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CN2-87) Around 15,000 ha (58 sq mi) of banana crop was wiped out.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CN10-88) In all, the municipalities of Ixtlahuacán, [Tecomán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tecom%C3%A1n "Tecomán"), Manzanillo, and Comala Coquimatlán sustained the worst effects from Manuel in the state.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CN7-89) Manuel was considered the worst storm to hit the Mexican state since the [1959 Mexico hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Mexico_hurricane "1959 Mexico hurricane").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CN9-90) Damage in the state exceeded $479 million pesos ($36.8 million 2013 USD).[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CN12-91)

### Jalisco

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hurricane_Manuel&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Jalisco")]

Further north, minor flooding was reported in [Jalisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalisco "Jalisco").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU42-92) Statewide, four people were killed. A 26-year-old man died after being swept away by in the village of [Juanacatlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juanacatlan "Juanacatlan") while a 12-year-old boy drowned after falling in a dam in the municipality of [Teocuitatlan de Corona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teocuitatlan_de_Corona "Teocuitatlan de Corona"). Another man perished when he drove his car into a ravine in [Cuautitlan de Garcia Barragan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuautitlan_de_Garcia_Barragan "Cuautitlan de Garcia Barragan"). Fifteen hundred people were evacuated from their homes. Classes were briefly cancelled in 588 schools, leaving over 40,000 pupils home. Bridges collapsed in the Jalisco towns of [Zacoalco de Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zacoalco_de_Torres "Zacoalco de Torres") and [Tamazula de Gordiano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamazula_de_Gordiano "Tamazula de Gordiano"). The worst-hit areas in the state were the southern and coastal areas of the state, as well as the [Guadalajara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalajara "Guadalajara") area, where flooding and landslides occurred in some neighborhoods.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-93) Through Jalisco, 56 municipalities sustained damage.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU36-94)

### Sinaloa

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hurricane_Manuel&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Sinaloa")]

Just before its second landfall, one fisherman was killed in [Tepechitlán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tepechitl%C3%A1n "Tepechitlán").[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU23-95) Another casualty occurred when a person fell off a shrimp boat.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU51-96) A truck driver and a 5 year old also died, while the toddler's mother was considered missing.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU37-97) The towns of [Escuinapa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escuinapa_de_Hidalgo "Escuinapa de Hidalgo"), [El Rosario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Rosario,_Baja_California "El Rosario, Baja California"), and Mazatlán,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-NPR-36) as well as the municipalities of [Angostura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angostura,_Sinaloa "Angostura, Sinaloa"), [Mocorito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mocorito "Mocorito"), Navolato, and [Culiacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culiac%C3%A1n "Culiacán") sustained flooded, resulting in modest damage. In Angostura, numerous people were trapped on the roofs of their houses. Coastal areas of Navolato were flooded while authorities reported 500 homeless;[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU34-98) hundreds of threes were toppled and power lines were disconnected.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU35-99) Parts of Mocorito were isolated due to overflow of the Humaya channel.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU34-98) About 2 m (6.6 ft) of water and debris was reported in Mocorito.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU52-100) In Culiacán, minor flooding happened.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU34-98) Meanwhile, in Chinito, almost all roads were destroyed.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU36-94) Offshore, 24 boats were damaged.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CNN2-101) Throughout the state, 100,000 people were rendered as homeless.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU37-97) A total of 3,000 persons were evacuated to 62 shelters. In all, 70 communities were damaged by the tropical cyclone.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CNN2-101) Hurricane Manuel directly affected 146,000 persons in 10 municipalities in the state.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU39-102) Damage in Sinaloa totaled $500 million pesos ($37.9 million 2013 USD).[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU49-103)

### Elsewhere

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hurricane_Manuel&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Elsewhere")]

Elsewhere, in [Michoacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michoac%C3%A1n "Michoacán"), flooding was reported; many people had to be rescued via air[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU24-104) and two casualties were reported.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CF-58) In [Durango](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durango "Durango"), 42 homes were damaged,[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU16-105) stranding 50 residents.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU38-56) While brushing the [Baja California Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baja_California_Peninsula "Baja California Peninsula"), 2 ft (0.61 m) waves were measured in [La Paz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Paz,_Baja_California_Sur "La Paz, Baja California Sur") in addition to winds of 26 mph (42 km/h).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU46-30) In Sinaloa, a peak rainfall total of 415 mm (15 in) was recorded at Culiacán.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU37-97) After dissipating, the remnants of Manuel brought copious amounts of rainfall to a wide swath of Texas.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-NWSBRO-106) The precipitation was further enhanced by deepening moisture from the Gulf of Mexico and an approaching [cold front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_front "Cold front").[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-NASASees-107) In the [Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin,_Texas "Austin, Texas") area, the rains resulted in localized flooding, forcing the closure of several [low water crossings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_water_crossing "Low water crossing"). A weather station in [Camp Mabry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Mabry "Camp Mabry") recorded 2.92 in (74 mm) of rain on September 20, making it a daily record for the station.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-ATXFlood-108) Elsewhere, radar estimates indicated that as much as 8 in (200 mm) may have fallen in localized areas in [West Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Texas "West Texas").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-NWSBRO-106) In [Kimble County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimble_County,_Texas "Kimble County, Texas"), one road was closed due to flooding. Across central [Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas "Arkansas"), 2–4.5 in (51–114 mm) of rainfall was recorded.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-109)

During the aftermath of the storm, a [state of emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_emergency "State of emergency") was declared for Acapulco;[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU11-129) about 12,000 items were airlifted to the region. overall.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU26-130) In all, 662 donation centers were opened across Guerrero.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU25-63) Damages repairs to Guerrero totaled to $3 billion MXN ($123 million 2013 USD).[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU14-131) The Minister of Economy granted an additional $100 million pesos to the devastated state.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU45-132) Furthermore, the Finance Ministry declared it had $12 billion pesos (US$925.60 million) available in funds.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-NBCN-52) In addition, the [Mexican Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Red_Cross "Mexican Red Cross") collected and subsequently delivered cargo to the devastated area, especially Guerrero[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW5-59) while also providing 400,079 tons of aid. Local authorities also provided 29,000 tons of personal and household items.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW21-133) The Médicos Sin Fronteras distributed 2,800[L](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Litre "Litre") (620[imp gal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_gallon "Imperial gallon")) of water, food, and medicines in five shelters.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW5-59) A total of 87 million [Euros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euros "Euros") (US$118 million), from the National Fund for Natural Disasters, were allocated to provide essential items such as food, mattresses, drinking water, and medicine.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW6-134) The Water Missions International provided water to about 20,000 persons.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW9-135) World Vision Mexico disturbed plastic tends to help cover roofs for 80 families. Furthermore, the organization donated mosquito nets for 76 families. Grocery items such as rice, oil, sardines, sugar, salt, cookies, and beans were also provided.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW10-136)[ADRA Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adventist_Development_and_Relief_Agency_International "Adventist Development and Relief Agency International") was one of the first organizations to help victims, and by early October, had helped 8,000 people.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW17-137)

In Oaxaca, 42 municipalities were declared disaster areas.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU15-138) Throughout the state of Guerrero, 56 municipalities were declared a disaster area[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU20-139) while 9 municipalities in Michoacán were declared a disaster zone.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU19-140) In all, 428 municipalities were designated as disaster areas[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-SG-141) and 155 emergencies declarations were issued due to both Ingrid and Manuel.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-CNN3-55) State of emergencies were declared in Michoacán and 21 municipalities in Jalisco, though by mid-October, they were lifted.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW22-142)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW23-143)

Thirty-two damage assessment committees were installed to help estimate and analyze the cost of damage to public infrastructure. Subcommittees were established to help assess damage to schools, houses, and water supplies.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-SG-141) Ten shelters were opened in both Chilpancingo and Acapulco.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU7-71)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU9-144) All survivors form the La Pintada mudslide were transported to a basketball gym in [Acapulco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acapulco "Acapulco"), who were all provided with a US$150 pension.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-BBC_2-61) Due to the closure of the commercial terminal of the Acapulco airport, special flights provided by Aeroméxico and Interjet were used to deliver aid.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW7-65)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Deslave_Carretera_Pie_de_la_Cuesta%2C_Sep_2013.jpg/250px-Deslave_Carretera_Pie_de_la_Cuesta%2C_Sep_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Deslave_Carretera_Pie_de_la_Cuesta,_Sep_2013.jpg)

Landslide in the highway Acapulco–[Pie de la Cuesta, Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pie_de_la_Cuesta,_Guerrero "Pie de la Cuesta, Guerrero")

By September 18, power services had been restored to the state of Guerrero.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU27-145) That day, gas and water services were revived in Acapulco.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU44-146) Emergency declarations were requested in Angostura and Navolato.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU33-147) Within 12 hours after its second landfall, power was retrieved to 26,000 dwellings in Sinaloa.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU31-148) In La Pintada, the search process for victims was halted briefly due to the threat of another mudslide,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW7-65) but on September 20, 100 rescuers resumed searching, who frequently had to dig through mud to recover bodies.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW8-67)

The Mexican government received criticism by the press for being under-prepared for both Manuel and Ingrid. One newspaper said that the authorities underestimated both storms, due to a combination of a "lack of coordination" and "the distraction of the weekend's independence-related festivities."[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-TT-62) Guerrero governor [Angel Aguirre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81ngel_Aguirre_Rivero "Ángel Aguirre Rivero") was criticized by many for attending a night-long party and drinking when the storm first threatened the state. However, Aguirre later acknowledged political corruption, as well as the construction of homes and hotels in unsafe areas in a televised speech. Consequently, the [Mexican Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Senate "Mexican Senate") requested an investigation in the amount of preparation that occurred.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-UPI-149)

To cope with relief efforts, Mexican Army troops and marines forces helped families whose homes were flooded.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU1-74) Additionally, the military provided 60 tonnes (132,275 lb) of food supplies and 8,000 litres (1,760 imp gal) of water to the city.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW3-150) A military airbase was installed to transport aid via air.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-EU9-144) Authorities rushed to clean rocks and other debris from two highways in order to liberate Acapulco from isolation.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW4-64) The disaster also resulted in [panic buying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panic_buying "Panic buying") at supermarkets.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-RW4-64) Looters were spotted in Acapulco many angry victims robbed shops, homes, luxury hotels, and apartments. Marines were posted outside stores to prevent further theft.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-NBCN-52) Mexico President [Enrique Peña Nieto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enrique_Pe%C3%B1a_Nieto "Enrique Peña Nieto") toured through most of the devastated areas, promising to rebuild La Pintada and Acapulco.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-BBC-151) On May 26,2014, La Pintada was re-opened, with 125 new homes.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-YE-66)

Because of the severe damage caused by the storm in Mexico, the name _Manuel_ was [retired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_retired_Pacific_hurricane_names "List of retired Pacific hurricane names") by the [World Meteorological Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Meteorological_Organization "World Meteorological Organization") following the 2013 season, and will never be used again for an eastern Pacific tropical cyclone. It was replaced with _Mario_ for the [2019 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Pacific_hurricane_season "2019 Pacific hurricane season").[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel#cite_note-152)

Part of the **[2015 Pacific hurricane season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Pacific_hurricane_season "2015 Pacific hurricane season")**

**Hurricane Patricia** was the most powerful [tropical cyclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone "Tropical cyclone") on record worldwide in terms of [maximum sustained winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_sustained_winds "Maximum sustained winds"). It was also the second-most intense on record worldwide in terms of pressure, with a minimum [atmospheric pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmospheric_pressure "Atmospheric pressure") of 872 mbar (25.75 inHg), just behind [Typhoon Tip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon_Tip "Typhoon Tip")'s 870 mbar (25.69 inHg).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-TCR-1) Originating from a sprawling disturbance near the [Gulf of Tehuantepec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Tehuantepec "Gulf of Tehuantepec"), south of Mexico, in mid-October 2015, Patricia was first classified as a [tropical depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_depression "Tropical depression") on October 20. Initial development was slow, with only modest strengthening within the first day of its classification. The system later became a tropical storm and was named Patricia, the twenty-fourth named storm of the [2015 Pacific hurricane season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Pacific_hurricane_season "2015 Pacific hurricane season"). Exceptionally favorable environmental conditions fueled [explosive intensification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_intensification "Rapid intensification") on October 22. A well-defined [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_(cyclone) "Eye (cyclone)") developed within an intense [central dense overcast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_dense_overcast "Central dense overcast") and Patricia grew from a tropical storm to a [Category 5 hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffir%E2%80%93Simpson_scale#Category_5 "Saffir–Simpson scale") in just 24 hours—a near-record pace. On October 23, the hurricane achieved its record peak intensity with [maximum sustained winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_sustained_wind "Maximum sustained wind") of 215 mph (345 km/h).[[nb 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-2)[[nb 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-3) This made it the most intense tropical cyclone on record in the [Western Hemisphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Hemisphere "Western Hemisphere") and the strongest globally in terms of one-minute maximum sustained winds.

Late on October 23, dramatic weakening ensued and Patricia made [landfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landfall "Landfall") near Cuixmala, [Jalisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalisco "Jalisco"), with winds of 150 mph (240 km/h). This still made it the strongest landfalling Pacific hurricane on record at the time, until it was surpassed by [Hurricane Otis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Otis "Hurricane Otis") in 2023. Patricia continued to weaken extremely quickly, faster than it had intensified, as it interacted with the mountainous terrain of Mexico. Within 24 hours of moving ashore, Patricia weakened into a tropical depression and dissipated soon thereafter, late on October 24.

The precursor to Patricia produced widespread flooding rains in Central America. Hundreds of thousands of people were directly affected by the storm, mostly in [Guatemala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemala "Guatemala"). At least six fatalities were attributed to the event: four in [El Salvador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Salvador "El Salvador"), one in Guatemala, and one in [Nicaragua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicaragua "Nicaragua"). Torrential rains extended into southeastern Mexico, with areas of [Quintana Roo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quintana_Roo "Quintana Roo") and [Veracruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veracruz "Veracruz") reporting accumulations in excess of 19.7 in (500 mm). Damage in [Chetumal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chetumal "Chetumal") reached [MX$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_peso "Mexican peso")1.4 billion (US$85.3 million).[[nb 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-4)

As a tropical cyclone, Patricia's effects in Mexico were tremendous; however, the affected areas were predominantly rural, lessening the number of people directly impacted. Violent winds tore roofs from structures and stripped coastal areas of their vegetation. Preliminary assessments indicated hundreds of homes were destroyed; seven fatalities were linked to the hurricane directly or indirectly, including one during evacuations. Total damage from Patricia was estimated to be at least $462.8 million (2015 [USD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")); the damage in Mexico alone was estimated to be in excess of MX$5.4 billion (US$325 million), with agriculture and infrastructure comprising the majority of losses. Flooding partially associated with remnant moisture from Patricia inflicted US$52.5 million in damage across [Southern Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Texas "South Texas").

On October 11, 2015, an area of disturbed weather traversed Central America and emerged over the eastern Pacific Ocean. The disturbance moved slowly over the next few days, later merging with a [tropical wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_wave "Tropical wave") on October 15. The merger of these systems and the effects of a concurrent [Tehuantepec gap wind event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehuantepecer "Tehuantepecer") spurred the formation of a broad [area of low pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-pressure_area "Low-pressure area"). This feature gradually consolidated and became a [tropical depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_depression "Tropical depression") shortly after 00:00[UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time "Coordinated Universal Time") on October 20; at this time the depression was situated roughly 205 mi (330 km) south-southeast of [Salina Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salina_Cruz "Salina Cruz"), Mexico. A [mid-level ridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ridge_(meteorology) "Ridge (meteorology)") to the north steered the depression generally west and later pulled it north along an arcing path.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-TCR-1)

Development was initially slowed by locally cooler [sea surface temperatures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_surface_temperature "Sea surface temperature") and dry air, and the depression became Tropical Storm Patricia later that day.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-TCR-1) Once clear of the unfavorable region, Patricia traversed anomalously warm waters within an environment exceptionally conducive to [rapid intensification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_intensification "Rapid intensification").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-TCR-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-5) Dramatic strengthening began late on October 21 and continued through October 23. Patricia reached [hurricane strength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category_1_hurricane "Category 1 hurricane") shortly after 00:00 UTC on October 22,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-TCR-1) featuring prominent [outflow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outflow_(meteorology) "Outflow (meteorology)"), well-defined banding features,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-D8-6) and a developing [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_(cyclone) "Eye (cyclone)").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-D7-7) Data from [hurricane hunters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_hunters "Hurricane hunters") investigating the cyclone indicated Patricia to have reached [Category 4 status](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category_4_hurricane "Category 4 hurricane") on the [Saffir–Simpson hurricane wind scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffir%E2%80%93Simpson_hurricane_wind_scale "Saffir–Simpson hurricane wind scale") by 18:00 UTC.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-TCR-1)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-D10-8)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cf/Hurricane_Patricia_October_23%2C_2015%2C_GOES-15_visible_animation.gif/250px-Hurricane_Patricia_October_23%2C_2015%2C_GOES-15_visible_animation.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hurricane_Patricia_October_23,_2015,_GOES-15_visible_animation.gif)

Satellite animation of Patricia weakening considerably before making landfall on October 23

By the early hours of October 23, a clear northward turn took place followed by acceleration northeast.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-D11-9) A solid ring of −130°F (−90°C) cloud tops surrounded the hurricane's 12 mi (19 km) wide eye and signaled its intensification into a [Category 5 hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category_5_hurricane "Category 5 hurricane"). In a 24-hour time span, Patricia's [maximum sustained winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_sustained_wind "Maximum sustained wind") increased by 120 mph (195 km/h), the fastest such intensification in any hurricane observed by the [National Hurricane Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hurricane_Center "National Hurricane Center") (NHC). The hurricane reached its peak intensity at around 12:00 UTC on October 23, with estimated winds around 215 mph (346 km/h) and a [barometric pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barometric_pressure "Barometric pressure") of 872 mbar (hPa; 25.75 inHg); these values are based upon continued intensification after a [Hurricane Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Hunter "Hurricane Hunter") mission into the storm six hours prior. In the NHC's report on Patricia, it is noted that the hurricane may have surpassed [Typhoon Tip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon_Tip "Typhoon Tip") as the strongest tropical cyclone ever observed, but lack of direct observations at the time of its peak prevents analysis of such.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-TCR-1)

Later on October 23, rapid weakening ensued as an [eyewall replacement cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyewall_replacement_cycle "Eyewall replacement cycle") took shape and wind shear increased. In the five hours up until [landfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landfall "Landfall") in Mexico, Patricia weakened at an unprecedented rate while still over water. However, upon moving ashore around 23:00 UTC near Cuixmala, Jalisco, it remained a strong Category 4 hurricane, with sustained winds of 150 mph (240 km/h) and an analyzed pressure of 932 mbar (hPa; 27.52 inHg). This made Patricia the most intense landfalling Pacific hurricane on record, until [Hurricane Otis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Otis "Hurricane Otis") surpassed it in October 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-OTIS-10) Once onshore, the high terrain of the [Sierra Madre mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Madre_Occidental "Sierra Madre Occidental") accelerated Patricia's weakening. The low- and mid-level circulations of the tropical cyclone decoupled, with the latter accelerating northeast, and Patricia dissipated on October 24 over central Mexico, less than 18 hours after moving ashore.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-TCR-1)

Hurricane Patricia set multiple records for maximum strength, rate of intensification, and rate of weakening throughout its relatively short existence. With maximum sustained winds of 215 mph (345 km/h) and a minimum pressure of 872 mbar (hPa; 25.75 inHg), Patricia is the [most intense tropical cyclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tropical_cyclone_records "List of tropical cyclone records") ever observed in the [Western Hemisphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Hemisphere "Western Hemisphere"). In terms of central pressure, it is also the second-most intense tropical cyclone ever recorded worldwide, just shy of [Typhoon Tip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon_Tip "Typhoon Tip") in 1979 which had a minimum pressure of 870 mbar (hPa; 25.69 inHg).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-TCR-1)

Patricia's one-minute maximum sustained winds ranked as the highest ever reliably observed or estimated in a tropical cyclone, surpassing [Typhoon Haiyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon_Haiyan "Typhoon Haiyan") of 2013.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-StrongestWHem-15) The magnitude of Patricia's rapid intensification is among the fastest ever observed. In a 24-hour period, 06:00–06:00 UTC October 22–23, its maximum sustained winds increased from 85 mph (140 km/h) to 205 mph (335 km/h), a record increase of 120 mph (195 km/h). During the same period, Patricia's central pressure fell by 95 mbar (hPa; 2.81 inHg). Despite record over-water weakening prior to striking Mexico, Patricia became the most intense Pacific hurricane to make landfall, with a pressure of 932 mbar (hPa; 27.52 inHg),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-TCR-1) until Otis surpassed this intensity with a pressure of 929 mbar (hPa; 27.43 inHg).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-OTIS-10)

### Forecast errors

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hurricane_Patricia&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Forecast errors")]

See also: [Meteorological history of Hurricane Patricia §Forecast errors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meteorological_history_of_Hurricane_Patricia#Forecast_errors "Meteorological history of Hurricane Patricia")

The rapid intensification of Patricia was well-anticipated but poorly forecasted. Meteorologists at the NHC indicated the possibility of such in the system's first advisory as a tropical depression. They noted the only inhibiting factor would be how quickly the storm could organize an inner core.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-TCR-1) Just before the onset of rapid intensification, the agency was unable to utilize the [Statistical Hurricane Intensity Prediction Scheme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone_forecast_model#Statistical_guidance "Tropical cyclone forecast model") rapid intensification guidance due to technical errors. This likely contributed to even greater errors in the agency's forecast.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-TCR-1) Initial forecasts were consistently conservative with intensity and dramatic strengthening was not explicitly shown until rapid intensification was already underway.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-TCR-1)

## Preparations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hurricane_Patricia&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Preparations")]

[President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Mexico "President of Mexico")[Enrique Peña Nieto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enrique_Pe%C3%B1a_Nieto "Enrique Peña Nieto") meets with [cabinet members](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Mexico "Cabinet of Mexico") to discuss Hurricane Patricia on October 23

Before Hurricane Patricia arrived, the [Government of Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Mexico "Government of Mexico") issued multiple [watches and warnings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone_warnings_and_watches "Tropical cyclone warnings and watches") for coastal communities. A [hurricane watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_watch "Hurricane watch") was first raised at 09:00 UTC on October 21, encompassing areas of [Michoacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michoac%C3%A1n "Michoacán"), [Colima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colima "Colima"), and [Jalisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalisco "Jalisco"). A [tropical storm watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_storm_watch "Tropical storm watch") also covered portions of [Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerrero "Guerrero"). As Patricia intensified, the government issued a [hurricane warning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone_warnings_and_watches "Tropical cyclone warnings and watches") for areas between [Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabo_Corrientes,_Jalisco "Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco"), and Punta San Telmo, Michoacán; a [tropical storm warning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_storm_warning "Tropical storm warning") supplemented this for areas farther north and east. The hurricane warning was extended northward to include areas south of [San Blas, Nayarit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Blas,_Nayarit "San Blas, Nayarit"), on October 23. Once the storm moved inland and the threat of damaging winds diminished, these warnings were gradually discontinued on October 24.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-TCR-1)

Following Patricia's upgrade to Category 5 status, the National Hurricane Center called the storm "potentially catastrophic",[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-16) a source of criticism and praise from various media.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-Forbes1-17) Citing the relatively limited damage and loss of life, some outlets, including the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-18) claimed the agency was exaggerating the danger posed by the storm. However, most outlets praised them for effectively communicating the dire threat and potentially saving lives from an exceptionally powerful hurricane.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-Forbes1-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia#cite_note-19)
